scenarios.title: Support the carrier after a give-and-go look
scenarios.objective: Keep supporting when the first pass changes the puck carrier and the return lane is shaded.
scenarios.briefing: Navy attacks +x. YOU has just passed to F2 near the right side; D1 shades the old return line between you. F1 is below the play and can become a third option.
cues: D1 shades the old return line.
F1 is a visible alternate support player.

questions.prompt: What changed when the pass reached F2?

options.text: F2 became the puck carrier
YOU became the puck carrier again
D1 became a teammate

questions.explanation: The setup assigns the puck to F2, so YOU's job is now support and scanning.

questions.prompt: Which two details should shape your next support spot?

options.text: F2's current puck position
D1's relationship to the old return line
Where the earlier pass started, without checking the new carrier

questions.explanation: The new carrier and the defender's shaded line explain why support must move; a return is only one possible continuation.

questions.prompt: Arrange this post-pass support read.

options.text: Find F2 and the shaded line
Move to a reachable new angle
Re-check F2, D1 and F1

questions.explanation: Support follows the actual carrier and the current coverage, with F1 available if the picture changes.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to a new support angle above the old return line.
questions.explanation: This point changes the relationship to D1 and F2 while leaving F1 separate; F2 may carry or pass based on the next read.

questions.prompt: F2 carries toward the middle instead of returning. What should YOU do?

options.text: Adjust support relative to F2 and call the available lane
Follow F2’s route without checking D1’s new lane
Hold the old return point without checking F2’s route

questions.explanation: Support follows the actual carrier. Update F2’s route and D1’s lane instead of chasing blindly or holding the old return point.

questions.prompt: What can your support accomplish when F2 keeps the puck?
questions.explanation: It can pull D1, offer a second lane, or protect F2's next option. Describe the named space and make the benefit conditional on D1's response.

scenarios.title: Reset behind a closing forechecker
scenarios.objective: Offer a reset behind pressure while preserving a forward option.
scenarios.briefing: Navy attacks +x. F1 controls the puck at the right half wall; D1 pressures from the inside and D2 is above the play. YOU is ahead of F1 and can slide behind the pressure for a reset.
cues: F1 is pressured at the half wall.
YOU can offer space behind F1.
D2 may change the reset lane.

questions.prompt: Where is the puck carrier in this freeze?

options.text: F1 at the half wall
YOU in the neutral zone
D2 above the play

questions.explanation: The puck owner is F1 at the half wall; YOU and the defenders are options and pressure, not the carrier.

questions.prompt: Which two features make a reset offer usable?

options.text: F1 can see and reach the offer
The offer stays separated from D1 and D2
The reset name matters more than the space around F1

questions.explanation: A reset is helpful because it is reachable and safer from pressure; if either cue changes, another route may be better.

questions.prompt: Arrange this conditional reset plan.

options.text: Read F1's pressure and the defenders
Move behind the pressure with separation
Re-check the reset and forward lanes

questions.explanation: The movement creates an option; the final scan decides whether F1 uses it, carries, or protects.

questions.prompt: Move YOU behind F1 and toward the middle to show a separated reset lane.
questions.explanation: This point moves behind the carrier and away from D1, while keeping D2 in view. A different open support point can also work.

questions.prompt: D2 drops into the reset lane. What should F1 and YOU revisit?

options.text: The remaining support and whether a protected carry is safer
The same backward pass as if D2 had not moved
A direct pass through D2

questions.explanation: D2 removed the offered lane, so re-scan the carrier's space, F1, and any other support before choosing.

questions.prompt: What would you communicate while offering this reset?
questions.explanation: Call the pressure and show that the reset is available only while the lane stays clear. If D2 closes it, name another support or carry space instead.

scenarios.title: Track the second bounce
scenarios.objective: Read a rebound location and the defender before choosing a follow-up route.
scenarios.briefing: Navy attacks +x. A shot has already been taken in this practice rep; the puck is loose below the right circle. YOU is the closest navy skater, F1 is above the puck, and D1 is between the puck and the net.
cues: The puck is loose below the right circle.
D1 is between the puck and the net.
F1 is higher and may become support after control.

questions.prompt: Where is the loose puck relative to the right net?

options.text: Below the circle
Behind the left net
With F1

questions.explanation: The puck is below the net-side circle and has no owner.

questions.prompt: Which two cues should guide your approach?

options.text: D1's position between puck and net
F1's higher support position
The shot guarantees a second attempt

questions.explanation: The defender and support locations explain the approach. A rebound still requires a new scan after control.

questions.prompt: Arrange this rebound-read routine.

options.text: Find the puck and defender
Approach under control
Re-check net space and F1

questions.explanation: The route begins with the visible puck and coverage, then updates after the approach; the follow-up remains a new choice.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to an inside approach point near the loose puck that keeps the right net and D1 visible.

questions.prompt: D1 reaches the puck first. What should you update?

options.text: Whether to support F1 or pressure the new carrier
Assume your second shot is still available
Chase the loose puck as if D1 had not reached it first

questions.prompt: What would you need to see before suggesting a second shot?

scenarios.title: Protect on the outside shoulder
scenarios.objective: Use your body position to keep a carrier option while pressure closes from inside.
scenarios.briefing: Navy attacks +x. YOU carries near the right-side lane with D1 inside and F2 higher in the middle. The practice constraint is one controlled touch before choosing to protect, carry, or use F2.
cues: YOU carries near the right-side lane.
F2 is a higher middle option.

scenarios.title: Carry into the quiet lane
scenarios.objective: Use open space while checking whether the defender can close the next carrying lane.
scenarios.briefing: Navy attacks +x. YOU has the puck in the neutral zone; D1 is ahead and inside, while F2 is wide ahead. The rep includes a small-area rule: take one controlled touch before deciding whether to continue the carry.
cues: Open space is ahead of YOU.
F2 is wide ahead, but the lane can change.
